title: Broad Lean Corpus Build and Rich Isomorphism Status v0

canonical_node.axiom: The broader Lean corpus contains a richer structural testing layer beyond equation-shape analogy, and its full build passes locally without active proof escapes.
definitions: Rich isomorphism: a mapping that preserves roles, transitions, signature discipline, gate behavior, and passes adversarial wrong-swap checks.
Proof escape: active use of sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in source files, excluding expected #check_failure diagnostics.
Seed kernel: a clean compressed assumption spine with 4 front-loaded assumptions and 17 no-sorry starter theorems.
Broad corpus: a richer formal archive with reported 287 theorems, zero sorry, zero admit, and adversarial proof surface.
derivation: The full build command 'lake build' completed successfully with 17 jobs.
The proof-escape scan found no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in main source files.
Targeted builds for Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, and other modules passed.
The corpus docs list RichLawIso, richLaw4Iso, no_rich_iso_to_natural_coin, richRelabeledCoinIso, BridgeMatrix, MasterEquationInvariance, and wrong-swap rejection rows.
The upgraded isomorphism layer requires role preservation, transition preservation, signature discipline, gate behavior, and adversarial wrong-swap failures.
The safe claim states that intended mappings pass inside the encoded model while selected false mappings fail.
canonical_node.action: Maintain the broad corpus as a separate build layer from the seed kernel, and continue to verify that the rich isomorphism layer is present and that the full build passes without active proof escapes.
boundary: Lean verifies the encoded structure but does not independently prove that every human label is domain-faithful.
Physics, theology, history, and source-grounding still carry the burden of domain faithfulness.
Do not dump the broad corpus into the seed package until the theorem inventory is normalized and wrapper/trivial rows are separated from substantive theorem rows.
test: Run 'lake build' and confirm it completes successfully.
Run the proof-escape scan and confirm no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in main source files.
Check that the rich isomorphism symbols and modules are present in the corpus.
Verify that the intended mappings pass and selected false mappings fail within the encoded model.

dg1_dependencies: Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, Theophysics_Coherence, Theophysics_Fracture, Theophysics_Fall, Theophysics_ChiEvaluator, Theophysics_NegativeInventory modules
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a richer structural testing layer (signature discipline, role/transition preservation, gate tests, adversarial wrong-swap checks) beyond simple equation-shape isomorphism.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: The seed kernel's clean compressed assumption spine and 17 no-sorry starter theorems remain intact as a separate build layer.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the rich isomorphism layer is removed, the framework would revert to relying merely on equation-shape analogy, losing the stronger structural testing and adversarial validation.

classification.claim_class: build status and structural capability claim
classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as a build-status and capability record; do not treat as a proof of domain faithfulness

overstatement_risks: Claiming that Lean proves domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Claiming that the rich isomorphism layer is equivalent to a full formal proof of the intended mappings.
Assuming the reported 287 theorems are all substantive without normalization.
kill_conditions: If the full build fails on a clean checkout.
If active sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe are found in main source files.
If the rich isomorphism symbols are absent from the corpus.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the rich isomorphism layer as a set of Lean theorems that verify role/transition preservation and signature discipline for the intended mappings, and prove that selected wrong-swap mappings fail.

plain_summary: This document reports that a broad Lean corpus builds successfully and contains a richer isomorphism layer with signature discipline and adversarial checks. It does not claim that Lean proves domain faithfulness; that remains a separate burden. The corpus should be kept separate from the seed kernel until the theorem inventory is normalized.
